paragraphs: On Thursday after lunch, the Explorers sat on big cushions in the school library. The cushions were very comfortable, and nobody wanted to move. Teacher Kim opened a cabinet and held up two small boxes. It was a long week, and she wanted a good program for everybody. "We have time for one program today," she said. "The first one is about a painter, and the second one is about sea animals." "Please tell me your opinion, and give me a reason." "Then we can discuss the programs together."

"I like the painter program," said Lily. "I think it is interesting, because the painter uses many colors." "I like how he mixes yellow and blue to make green." "It includes a short painting lesson, and we can try the same colors for the blog." "I do not agree," said Leo. "I think a painter program is boring, because he talks a lot and paints a little." "I want to watch the sea animals, because I love sharks."

"I agree with Leo," said Mia. "I need new animals for my fact files, and the sea program has many." "I agree with Lily," said May. "I draw at home every day, and I want to learn new ideas." "But I have a question." "How long is each program?" Teacher Kim looked at the back of the boxes. "The painter program is forty minutes, and the sea program is fifty minutes," she said. "We have only forty-five minutes in the library today."

"What a shame!" said Leo. "The sea program is too long, and I do not want to stop in the middle." "Then we can watch the painter program today," said May. "Next Thursday, we can watch the sea program, and we will have more time." "Is that fair?" asked Lily. "Yes, because both programs have a turn," said Mia.

Leo thought for a moment and then he nodded. "OK," he said. "I can wait, because the sharks will not go away." Teacher Kim put the sea box back in the cabinet. She started the painter program, and the room became quiet. The program began in a small room full of colors. The painter put one color on a big white paper. Nobody spoke for a long time. Lily smiled at Leo, and Leo smiled back. Everybody had an opinion, and everybody listened to the others.

sentences.text: On Thursday after lunch, the Explorers sat on big cushions in the school library.
The cushions were very comfortable, and nobody wanted to move.
Teacher Kim opened a cabinet and held up two small boxes.
It was a long week, and she wanted a good program for everybody.
"We have time for one program today," she said.
"The first one is about a painter, and the second one is about sea animals."
"Please tell me your opinion, and give me a reason."
"Then we can discuss the programs together."
"I like the painter program," said Lily.
"I think it is interesting, because the painter uses many colors."
"I like how he mixes yellow and blue to make green."
"It includes a short painting lesson, and we can try the same colors for the blog."
"I do not agree," said Leo.
"I think a painter program is boring, because he talks a lot and paints a little."
"I want to watch the sea animals, because I love sharks."
"I agree with Leo," said Mia.
"I need new animals for my fact files, and the sea program has many."
"I agree with Lily," said May.
"I draw at home every day, and I want to learn new ideas."
"But I have a question."
"How long is each program?"
Teacher Kim looked at the back of the boxes.
"The painter program is forty minutes, and the sea program is fifty minutes," she said.
"We have only forty-five minutes in the library today."
"What a shame!" said Leo.
"The sea program is too long, and I do not want to stop in the middle."
"Then we can watch the painter program today," said May.
"Next Thursday, we can watch the sea program, and we will have more time."
"Is that fair?" asked Lily.
"Yes, because both programs have a turn," said Mia.
Leo thought for a moment and then he nodded.
"OK," he said.
"I can wait, because the sharks will not go away."
Teacher Kim put the sea box back in the cabinet.
She started the painter program, and the room became quiet.
The program began in a small room full of colors.
The painter put one color on a big white paper.
Nobody spoke for a long time.
Lily smiled at Leo, and Leo smiled back.
Everybody had an opinion, and everybody listened to the others.
